title: A microVM silently drops its fifteenth shared disk
details:
The guest init walks its auxiliary disks with a fixed letter list, `_letters=(c d e f g h i j k l m n o p)` (`image/guest/init:236`). That covers `/dev/vdc` through `/dev/vdp`, which is fourteen devices, and `--repo`, `--snapshot` and `--image-store` all advance the same cursor.

Past the fourteenth the index reads off the end of the array. The script does not run under `set -u`, so the expansion is empty, the device path becomes `/dev/vd`, the `[ -b ]` test fails, and the loop moves on without printing anything.

Nothing on the host side caps the count. `fcconfig.Build` sizes the drive list from the spec, and no caller validates it, so `create` attaches fifteen drives, reports success, and hands back a sandbox missing one of the directories you asked for. A repo you expected at `~/<name>` is simply absent.

The Podman engine bind-mounts each share and has no such limit, so the same command line means different things on the two engines. Either reject the fifteenth share in `create` with a clear message, or extend the guest past `vdp`.
